title: The Fear of Man
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The fear of man is being ruled by human approval, rejection, shame, pressure, opinion, or threat more than by reverence for God. It turns people into masters the heart feels compelled to obey.
summary: The fear of man is being ruled by human approval, rejection, shame, pressure, opinion, or threat more than by reverence for God. It turns people into masters the heart feels compelled to obey.
christFocus: Jesus Christ frees His people from living for human approval by bringing them into acceptance before God. He teaches believers to fear God, confess Him openly, and follow Him even when rejected by others.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The fear of man lays a snare. It can make people silent when they should speak, dishonest when they should tell truth, compromising when they should obey, and anxious when they should trust God.

This fear may appear as people-pleasing, avoidance, control, shame, craving approval, or terror of rejection. It often feels normal because human opinion is visible and immediate, while faith requires trust in the unseen God.

Scripture does not call believers to despise people. Love for neighbor is good, but fear of man becomes sinful when people’s approval or anger rules the heart more than God’s Word.

Christ frees believers to live before the Father. Because they are accepted in Him, they do not need to be enslaved by every opinion, threat, or rejection. The fear of the Lord displaces the fear of man.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many believers are quietly controlled by fear of rejection. They hide convictions, tolerate sin, avoid confession, or perform for approval. This bondage can look polite while pulling the heart away from faithfulness.

This doctrine is especially important for the ashamed, rejected, church-hurt, or approval-starved. Christ offers a better identity than the unstable verdict of people.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Ask where human approval has more power over you than God’s Word. Confess people-pleasing, fear, and compromise. Practice obedience before God in small faithful steps, speak truth with love, and remember that in Christ you are held by a stronger approval than the world can give or take away.
